**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 24 already delivers the ASSIGN preferred position on all four elements:

- **24.1 (p0087)** — Customer has a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or an M&A successor (merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all/substantially all assets), conditioned only on prompt notice and assignee assumption. The "Affiliate" definition (1.1) is standard and not artificially narrow.
- **24.2 (p0088)** — Asymmetric in our favour: Vendor cannot assign, delegate material performance, or transfer by change of control without our consent, with reasonableness limited to capability/financial standing, plus an express bar on assigning to a direct Customer competitor.
- **24.3 (p0089)** — Confirmed this residual clause does **not** undercut 24.1: it opens "For other assignments," so mutual consent applies only to transfers outside the 24.1 carve-out, and it uses the favourable "not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" standard.
- **24.4 (p0090)** — Directly forecloses the walk-away risk: no Vendor right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control, plus a cooperation obligation for successor administration.
- **13.3 (p0050)** — Licence transfer tracks Section 24, so licence rights follow a permitted assignment rather than lapsing.

I also swept the full document for hidden triggers. The only other "assign"/"change of control" hits are 9.2 (mutual insolvency termination, with a helpful carve-out that lawful reorganization is not itself grounds for termination), 26.1 (assigned personnel) and 29.2 (notice formalities) — none creates a Vendor exit or re-pricing right on our change of control, and there is no "deemed an assignment" language anywhere.
